thread.title: Spotify IPO Begins Trading Near 166, Above Expected Range | Investor's Business Daily

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: Spotify IPO Begins Trading Near 166, Above Expected Range | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) commenced its uncommon initial public offering on Tuesday, with trading on the New York Stock Exchange starting near 165.90 per share, above its most recent pricing on private markets.

X That placed a valuation on the streaming music leader of $29 billion, compared with a previous high of about $23.5 billion.
Spotify is using a direct listing approach, an unconventional way to pursue an IPO, helping the company eliminate the need for a Wall Street bank or broker to underwrite the public offering, thus saving it costly service fees. As a direct listing, its opening public price was determined by orders collected by the NYSE from broker-dealers.
Shares ended their first regular session at 149.01,up nearly 13% from the reference price of 132. Spotify chose electronic-trading firm Citadel Securities to oversee its trading debut.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Spotify's March 23 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission says that from Jan. 1 through March 9, shares traded privately in a range of 48.93 to 132.50. The company is expected to offer up to 55.7 million ordinary shares.
Largest Streaming Service? Spotify says it's the largest global music streaming subscription service. It has 159 million monthly active users and 71 million subscribers for its premium service package. The company says it's nearly double the scale of its closest competitor, the Apple Music platform from Apple ( AAPL ). Apple Music recently disclosed having 38 million paying subscribers.
Spotify's other competitors include Google Play Music, owned by Alphabet ( GOOGL ), and Pandora ( P ). Spotify will also compete with Amazon ( AMZN ) and its Amazon Music platform. Alphabet is reportedly picking a fight with Apple, Pandora and Spotify with a new music streaming service, after squaring off with Amazon.
Sweden-based Spotify expects to have 198 million to 208 million monthly active users by the end of 2018. That includes paid and free users, an increase of about 29% from the year-ago period. It expects 2018 revenue in the range of $6.1 billion to $6.8 billion.
